text:
maria-support: Customer on Node 20 + Lambda seeing duplicate POSTs when our TS SDK retries. Customer says they get two identical charges in their downstream system. Repro steps attached.

jake-engruntime: ack, can you paste the minimal repro and the SDK/undici versions?

maria-support: SDK v1.2.0, undici v5.8.0, Node 20 on Lambda. Repro snippet:
```js
const ac = new AbortController();
await client.post('/generate', { body: streamBody, signal: ac.signal, retry: true });
// lib retries inside SDK when timeout happens
```
They run in a short-lived Lambda (cold starts), timeout triggers a retry and downstream sees duplicate POST.

emma-devex: short answer: using the same AbortController or a non-rewindable stream across retries can cause the request body to be sent twice (or not at all) depending on Undici behaviour. SDK 1.2.0 had a retry wrapper that reused the provided signal in some paths.

alex-sdk: looking into logs — support-ticket#2026-811 attached by support-bot. support-bot: <https://redwood.support/2026-811|ticket 2026-811> created and linked.

jake-engruntime: can you collect the request ids and the SDK debug logs? ask customer to set REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=1 and paste dumping of `requestId` + `retryAttempt` from our client logs. Also need undici pool logs if possible.

maria-support: pasted logs:
```
[2026-01-10T14:02:31Z] requestId=abc123 attempt=1 sending POST /charge id=tx-001
[2026-01-10T14:02:33Z] attempt=1 timed out, aborting signal
[2026-01-10T14:02:33Z] attempt=2 sending POST /charge id=tx-002
```
They show two distinct downstream transactions.

sre-oncall: quick hypothesis: Lambda freeze/unfreeze + reused undici pool + shared AsyncIterator stream + single AbortController = body already consumed, SDK may fall back to reserializing resulting in duplicate. Also older undici had buggy signal transfer semantics pre-5.12.

alex-sdk: confirmed a bug in SDK v1.2.0 where we sometimes reused the user's AbortSignal for retries instead of creating a fresh internal one, and we didn't clone non-rewindable bodies before re-sending. Repro is easy in Lambda.

emma-devex: mitigation for customers: 1) upgrade SDK to 1.3.4 (contains fix) and undici to >=5.14.2, 2) avoid passing user-managed AbortController into the call when you enable SDK-managed retries, or create a fresh AbortController per attempt, 3) for streams use a rewindable buffer or pre-buffer small payloads.

maria-support: asked customer to try upgrade and also send a patched call using per-attempt AC. They replied after testing: "upgraded to SDK 1.3.4 + undici 5.14.2, duplicate POSTs stopped."

jake-engruntime: final action items: - patch release note referencing PR #4123 - add unit test covering non-rewindable body retry in the SDK harness - add a debugging note in docs about AbortController + retries in Lambda.

support-bot: Created follow-up sprint ticket INF-788 with tasks and assigned to alex-sdk.

alex-sdk: PR merged, patch release 1.3.4 published. Closing ticket after 48h no-repro confirmation. :tada:

maria-support: closing loop with customer and offering 1 month credit for billing duplicate txs. Customer accepted.

sre-oncall: note to self — we should add a small telemetry flag when retries + non-rewindable body detected to surface to ops.

jake-engruntime: thanks everyone. short summary pinned to ticket: upgrade SDK+undici, avoid reusing AbortController for automatic retries, and buffer streams if you need guaranteed single-delivery.

maria-support: marking resolved. :white_check_mark:
